request: Batch three Epic 6 (Debt and hardening) tickets in one power cycle: T1 bound the slug quantifier in .claude/skills/harness/plan-store.mjs (named error, not ENAMETOOLONG); T3 generators stamp a derived do-not-edit header with the constitution byte-equality mirror exception; T5 declare a release model block in project.json and teach the standup skill to read it.
novelty_evidence: All three trace to docs/roadmap-execution-plan.md Epic 6 (T1/T3/T5) and backlog keys durable-plan-slug-guard-length-cap-low-8b21, generators-stamp-derived-header-vs-byte-equality-contracts-e9c1, release-model-in-project-json-drives-standup-recommendation-a4f2.
track_reason: Power batch-sprint chosen over 3x spec-entry to amortize the mechanical phases over three related, spec-committed Epic-6 debt tickets (human-confirmed option-2; sprint-planner proposal at .claude/state/sprint/debt-hardening-batch/proposal.json).

tickets.title: Bound the slug quantifier in plan-store.mjs
acs: assertSafeSlug rejects an over-length slug with a clean named error before any path construction (never surfaces ENAMETOOLONG)
a slug at the exact max length is accepted
existing SLUG_RE charset/traversal rejections remain intact (REJECT, never normalize)
tickets.done_record: assertSafeSlug enforces a length bound and the plan-store write path surfaces the named error to the caller

tickets.title: Generators stamp a derived do-not-edit header
acs: generated files carry a derived header that makes a hand-edit detectable
the constitution byte-equality mirrors do NOT carry a false do-not-edit banner (their live file is the source)
audit-baseline still passes byte-equality on the mirrors
tickets.done_record: generator emits the derived header; audit detects a stripped/edited header; the mirror exception is expressed explicitly
tickets.design_call: Which generated files get the header and how the constitution-mirror exception is expressed — collides with the byte-equality contract; this is the load-bearing spec decision.

tickets.title: Declare a release model in project.json and teach standup to read it
acs: project.json declares a `release` block (cicd_model, release_branch, release_trigger, release_cycle, consumer_upgrade_cadence)
standup's gather.mjs surfaces the release config and degrades gracefully when the block is absent (never throws)
the main-context recommendation becomes release-model-aware (Article II — helper gathers, main context decides)
tickets.done_record: project.json + src/project.template.json carry the release block; standup reads it; recommendation is regime-aware
tickets.design_call: Config schema (five knobs per backlog -a4f2 user verbatim) + optional completeness_gate sub-block; recommendation judgment stays in main context.
